The present note revisits Petojević’s work and provides simplified proofs of two of the results proved in that article. By streamlining the arguments, the note aims to make these properties more accessible and easier to apply in further studies.

This note revisits the generalized left factorial functions \(K_i(z)\) introduced by Petojević and examines several of their basic analytic properties from a streamlined point of view. In particular, it gives simplified proofs of two properties that had previously been established by more elaborate arguments, showing that these results follow naturally from the defining relations of the functions and from standard facts about the gamma function and related special functions.

The main purpose of the note is to address an open question posed by Petojević in 2006 concerning the nature of the functions \(K_i(z)\). By analyzing their functional relations and their dependence on classical transcendental functions, the note resolves this question and clarifies the extent to which the generalized left factorial functions behave like other well-known special functions. The answer shows that the functions \(K_i(z)\) possess a richer analytic structure than might first be expected from their factorial-like definition.

A further part of the discussion is devoted to the differential transcendence of the functions \(K_i(z)\). The note explains that these functions are not merely new variants of elementary or differentially algebraic functions; rather, they exhibit differential transcendence in an appropriate sense. This means that they do not satisfy any nontrivial algebraic differential equation over the relevant base field of functions. As a result, the generalized left factorial functions occupy a distinct position among special functions: they are closely connected to classical objects such as the gamma function, yet their analytic and algebraic behavior cannot be reduced to that of elementary or differentially algebraic functions.

Overall, the note both simplifies existing results and settles a previously unresolved problem. It thereby provides a clearer understanding of Petojević’s generalized left factorial functions \(K_i(z)\), highlighting their analytic continuation, their functional identities, and their differential-algebraic complexity.
